title: UPDATE: Thai Ctrl Bker:Econ Recovers, Baht Volatile In 07
text:
(This updates an item published at 1503 GMT with more comment from the central bank governor.)  

BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--Thailand's business sectors will face global currency market volatility until the end of next year, but growth in the local economy could recover before then, central bank Governor Pridiyathorn Devakula said.  

In a dinner speech late Thursday, Pridiyathorn said global capital flows in an out of Asia have kept the central bank busy several times this year already, intervening in foreign exchange markets sometimes almost 24 hours a day to reduce volatility in the baht.  

"The central bank will maintain its role of reducing baht volatility as much as it can, but exporters and other business sectors have to prepare themselves (for baht strength) because the dollar trend is weak," due to the massive U.S. current account deficit, he said.  

The dollar closed Thursday in Asia at THB37.685, up from a six-and-a-half-year low of THB37.28 Aug. 11, with help from heavy intervention by the Bank of Thailand last week.  

Pridiyathorn said the central bank can't work miracles to pin the baht down at one place, however, and it won't act against the trend.  

Thai businesses can expect foreign exchange volatility from swings in global capital flows to continue until the end of next year, he said. He didn't elaborate, but was apparently referring to adjustments global investors have been making in preparation for an imminent peak and a reversal likely next year in the U.S. interest rate cycle.  

While external volatility will remain a risk, however, local economic fundamentals are relatively stable, he said.  

Gross domestic product growth will likely slow to a range of 3%-4% on year in the second half of the year from an estimated 5.4% on year in the first half, for full-year 2006 growth of around 4.5%, he said.  

But GDP growth next year is likely to exceed 4.5% as pent-up investment surges after the formation of a new government, Pridiyathorn said.  

His figures were in line with the latest official central bank forecasts. Growth next year is projected in a range of 4%-5.25%.  

Growth has been slowing due to high oil prices and interest rates, and to slumping confidence in an extended period of political uncertainty.  

Thailand has been without a working legislature under a caretaker government since parliament was dissolved in February. The results of snap polls held April 2 were annulled due to irregularities. General elections scheduled Oct. 15 may be delayed while an Election Commission is chosen, but a new government is expected to be formed by late this year or early next year.  

Pridiyathorn said private investment will have to rise after political uncertainty eases, because capacity utilization has risen to 76%, where it stood before the Asian financial crisis of 1997.  

In the meantime, growth in investment and consumption will slow further, and exports will likely begin to slow if global demand eases as expected.  

But public spending is emerging to support the economy through the rough patch in the second half of this year, Pridiyathorn said.  

Due in part to the political uncertainty, public spending was down 0.3% on year in the first half, but the caretaker government has moved to accelerate spending under the current budget in the current third quarter of the calendar year, which is the final quarter of the fiscal year 2006, he said.  

In the coming quarter ending Dec. 31, 2006, the first quarter of fiscal 2007, the caretaker government plans to speed up carryover spending, and public spending is expected to rise 11% on year in the second half of the calendar year, he said.  

Later, Governor Pridiyathorn told reporters government spending can't be counted on as driver of growth next year. An expanded budget for the fiscal year beginning Oct. 1, 2006 probably won't be approved by a new parliament until the first or second quarter of the next calendar year.  

Exports have been the main engine of growth in 2006 and will continue to be the main driver next year, so the central bank can't let the baht strengthen too much, Pridiyathorn said.  

The Bank of Thailand does incur costs from issuing baht-denominated bonds to sterilize the effects on the local money supply of buying foreign currency to stem the baht's rise. However, the income from investing the increased foreign reserves is close to the interest cost of the bonds, there isn't much effect on the central bank, he said. The central bank's foreign reserves stood at $59.4 billion as of Aug. 11.  

Meanwhile, despite expectations both local and U.S. interest rates are at or near a peak and could begin falling next year, Pridiyathorn said he couldn't comment on the long-term outlook for Thai interest rates, because global oil prices continue fluctuating.

title: Thai Ctrl Bk Chief: Agrees With Fin Min's Baht Target
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--Thailand's central bank agrees with Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya's target level for the baht, Bank of Thailand Governor Pridiyathorn Devakula said Wednesday.  

Thanong earlier in the day said the appropriate dollar level for this year is between THB37.50 and THB38.00, while for next year it is around THB37.50.  

"If the finance minister said so, we have to believe him. Our view is in line with the finance ministry," Pridiyathorn told reporters. [ 23-08-06 0921GMT ]  

At Wednesday's close in Asia, the dollar was quoted at THB37.62, up from THB37.56 at Tuesday's close.  

The dollar dropped to a six-and-a-half-year low of THB37.28 on Aug. 11, and was only restrained from setting fresh lows last week by heavy central bank intervention.  

Pridiyathorn said the recent rise in Thailand's foreign reserves was mainly due to central bank intervention in the foreign exchange market, with the authority buying dollars to help curb the Thai baht's strength.  

As of Aug. 11, the country's foreign reserves stood at $59.4 billion with a net forward position of $5 billion.  

"Even though we have costs (from market intervention), this can be offset by returns from our higher foreign reserves," Pridiyathorn said.  

Sterilization of the increase in local money supply caused by dollar buying through issuance of baht-denominated bonds raises the central bank's interest costs, but these costs are offset by interest income on the higher foreign reserves. Dollar weakness against other key currencies has further boosted the foreign reserves in dollar terms, he added.  

The central bank earlier said its foreign reserves comprise many key currencies. It didn't elaborate.

title: Thai Fin Min:Baht Should Rise No More Than 3-3.5% Per Yr
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht should appreciate at no more than 3.0%-3.5% each year, a rate that will allow businesses to adapt comfortably to exchange-rate movements, Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said Wednesday.  

Thanong told reporters that the appropriate dollar level for this year is between THB37.50 and THB38.00, while that for next year is around THB37.50. [ 23-08-06 0406GMT ]  

The Bank of Thailand's recent intervention to curb the baht's strength is a short-term measure to prevent excessive inflows that might lead to a rapid rise in the currency's value, which would hurt the economy and exports, Thanong said.  

"The movement of the baht should be gradual. If it needs to be firmer, it should rise in steps," said Thanong.  

At 0410 GMT Wednesday, the dollar was at THB37.605, barely changed from THB37.61 early. It has weakened from THB41.025 at the beginning of this year.  

Thanong said the baht's firmer tone is in line with a regional trend doesn't substantially affect the country's competitiveness.  

Still, he expressed concerns over a possible slowdown in investment, which could weigh on economic growth.  

Many business operators have deferred their investments due to domestic political uncertainty and higher interest rates.  

"I personally expect economic growth this year to be between 4.2% and 4.5%, and next year between 3.75% and 4.0%," Thanong said.  

The ministry of finance's official growth forecast for this calendar year ranges from 4.0%-5.0%. The ministry hasn't yet issued its growth projection for next year.

title: Emerging Asia  FX -Pare losses, oil worries remain
text:
SINGAPORE, Aug 22 (Reuters) - Gains in regional stock markets helped Asian currencies trim losses on Tuesday but worries over high oil prices remained after Iran, the world's fourth-largest oil exporter, said it would press on with its nuclear programme.  

"Equities is one reason," said a trader in Singapore, referring to a recovery in Asian currencies. "There is also a lot of options-related trade going on today so that has been driving the market."  

The yen, which was weaker both against the U.S. dollar and the euro <EURJPY=>, also set the tone for Asian currencies. It was undermined by concerns over its low yields and widening interest rate differentials.  

The European Central Bank is expected to raise rates again after bringing rates up to 3 percent earlier this month, while the Bank of Japan is likely to lift rates only gradually after a rise to 0.25 percent last month, its first increase in six years.  

Oil traded above $72 per barrel on Tuesday after rising more than $1 on Monday. Iran is expected to respond on Tuesday to a package of incentives from the six world powers that aims to end a nuclear stand-off.  

Its commitment to its nuclear programme raised the prospect of U.N. sanctions being imposed on the country and of Iran using oil as a weapon in the row.  

"Oil prices are up again. It's quite uncertain so it's being a drag on Asian currencies," said Irene Cheung, a regional economist at ABN AMRO Bank.  

Apart from the yen factor, a dealer at a commercial bank in Thailand said the Thai baht <THB=> tested the downside after the Bank of Thailand intervened last week in the range of 37.40-37.45 per dollar to slow the currency's rise.  

The baht has been the strongest in the region this year, driven by foreign portfolio inflows, a strengthening current account and, more recently, signs of a resolution to the country's political stalemate.  

The market was looking forward to news by Thursday of the appointment of members of a new election commission that will pave the way for a general election on Oct. 15.  

"Failure to do so would risk a postponement of the October 15 election date, setting Thailand off its course to expeditiously settle the already long-drawn-out political standstill," UBS said in a note.  

The Taiwan dollar <TWD=TP> recovered after being down most of the day.  

"The stock market was up, volume was down but foreigners were selling, not buying any more," ABN AMRO's Cheung said.  

Taiwan had net equity outflows of $16.6 million for the first time in more than two weeks, stock exchange data showed.  

Nomura International said foreign investors were net buyers of $1.4 billion of Asian equities last week, the highest in 15 weeks. Only South Korea and the Philippines recorded net outflows. Foreign investors have been net sellers in South Korea for six weeks in a row, Nomura said.  

Cheung said the Taiwan dollar, which reached a one-week low of 32.774 per U.S. dollar, would remain pressured by local political problems as a campaign to oust Taiwan President Chen Shui-bian gathers steam.

title: Thai Baht Ends Down On Foreign Bks' Dlr Buying; Bonds Up
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht ended softer against the dollar Thursday on substantial buying of the U.S. currency by two major foreign banks, despite a generally bearish dollar tone, traders said.  

Government bond prices rose in line with overnight gains in U.S. Treasurys after an issue of data that indicated U.S. inflationary pressures are easing.  

The dollar ended at THB37.585, up from THB37.43 at the Asian close Wednesday, after moving in an intraday range of THB37.44 to THB37.62.  

Traders said the heavy dollar buying may simply have been profit-taking, or it could be linked to speculation that the acquisition of a controlling stake in Thai telecommunications conglomerate Shin Corp. PCL (SHIN.TH) by Singapore's Temasek Holding (TEMAH.YY) may be reversed if the commerce ministry rules that a local holding company involved in the deal is serving as a nominee for Temasek.  

The big dollar buying orders came from a U.S. bank and a Swiss-based bank, traders said.  

"It's not common to see any parties buying such a huge amount, especially while the overall dollar trend is softening... However, they didn't seem to be acting on behalf of the central bank as the authorities don't normally move this aggressively," one local trader said.  

Profit-taking would be a plausible explanation, as funds may have decided to sell off positions after failing to take the baht past resistance from Bank of Thailand interventions after the currency hit a 6.5-year high at THB37.28 against the dollar Friday.  

But renewed concerns about the Shin-Temasek deal may have contributed to the dollar buying.  

An initial investigation by the Commerce Ministry found evidence that the local Kularb Kaew Ltd. could be a nominee for Temasek, which would mean that the Singapore government investment arm owns a stake in Shin in excess of the limit on foreign ownership, Deputy Permanent Secretary for Commerce Yanyong Phuangrach told reporters Thursday.  

He said further information is needed before the ministry can reach a conclusion, however. The ministry will take around two months to finalize the matter and forward its findings to the police, who will consider whether to refer the case to court, Yanyong said.  

The findings aren't likely to have a long-term effect on the baht, however, because Yanyong said any confirmation that Kularb Kaew is a nominee for Temasek would only require that share holdings be adjusted, and any legal charges would be brought against the local holding company.  

Dollar selling by exporters around THB37.60 limited the U.S. unit's gains, providing immediate resistance.  

Dealers expect the dollar to find next firm resistance at THB37.80 while support is pegged at THB37.40. [ 17-08-06 1108GMT ]  

Thai government bond yields ended lower, tracking the reaction of U.S. Treasury yields to data issued overnight indicating U.S. inflation pressures are easing, dealers said.  

The average bid on the government bond due November 2009 eased almost 1/2 basis point to 5.296%, the July 2016 bid fell three basis points to 5.483% and the July 2026 bid was down one basis point to end at 5.789, according to the Web site of the Thai Bond Market Association.  

Yields were expected to remain range bound with limited room to decline due to stable money market interest rates.  

The most-active overnight interbank interest rate was expected to have remained around 4.95%.

title: Emerging Asia  FX -Thai baht restrained by  central bank
text:
SINGAPORE, Aug 16 (Reuters) - Asian currencies rose on Wednesday, some of them after several days of losses against the dollar, following soft U.S. producer price data that reduced expectations of further rate rises by the Federal Reserve.  

Extended declines in crude oil prices also inspired gains.  

The yen <JPY=> rallied more than half a percent to around 116 per dollar. The Singapore dollar <SGD=> and Philippine peso <PHP=> regained the quarter percent they lost on Tuesday.  

The Indonesian rupiah <IDR=> was flat around 9,100 a dollar.  

The baht <THB=> was among Wednesday's biggest gainers although its rise was thwarted by the Bank of Thailand's dollar-buying intervention.  

It was quoted around 37.32/35 per dollar, staying on the weaker side of Friday's 6-1/2-year high of 37.215 per dollar.  

Traders offered various reasons for the baht's 1.8 percent climb in the past 2 weeks, although the central bank attributed its rise to foreign inflows into Thai equity and bond markets.  

Some said Singapore state investment firm Temasek Holdings [TEM.UL] was repaying a baht loan taken earlier this year when it bought a stake in telecoms group Shin Corp . That loan was estimated to be about $1 billion.  

Another trader said the cash inflows into Thailand were to fund a likely sale of Bank of Ayudhya's 25 percent stake to General Electric .  

The Bank of Thailand's intervention confused traders, since the central bank had said earlier this month it would allow the currency to appreciate in line with market forces.  

"These are sort of lumpy flows which are not going to be sustainable," said Sriyan Pietersz, JPMorgan's chief Thai strategist.  

"While I do think we will see more foreign inflows on the equity side in the months to come, I don't think they are going to be that large," he said.  

Analysts also said that by intervening to rein in the baht, the central bank was helping Temasek get a better rate for its loan repayment.  

"The BOT's motive is to stop dollar/baht doing down. But by default, they end up pushing dollar/baht higher so it makes it cheaper for Temasek to buy baht," one analyst said.  

TAIWAN FLOWS  

Elsewhere, Taiwan's stock market <.TW11> rose 1.23 percent on the back of a heavy $312 million foreign net portfolio inflow. Yet, the currency <TWD=TP> was rangebound around 32.75 per U.S. dollar.  

Traders said more inflows into Asian markets were likely as the view that U.S. rates have peaked gets entrenched.  

U.S. core producer prices fell 0.3 percent in July from June, surprising analysts who had expected a rise. Consumer price inflation is due on Wednesday.  

"Any signs that the Fed was correct to pause this month will be taken as a positive for risky assets," ABN AMRO strategist Shahab Jalinoos said in a note.  

Asian currencies came under selling pressure earlier this week after robust U.S. retail sales data stoked expectations the Fed might renew a two-year tightening campaign after leaving rates unchanged last week.  

Crude oil, which the region imports in large quantities, fell below $73 a barrel after a U.N.-brokered truce ended fighting between Israel and Lebanon's Hizbollah.  

China's yuan <CNY=CFXS> also rose on Wednesday, recovering from the previous day's sharp fall to a three-week low.

text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht retreated Tuesday after the Bank of Thailand confirmed that it continued to intervene in foreign exchange markets to curb the baht's strength after it hit a six-and-a-half year high Friday, traders said.  

However, the baht's fall was limited by offshore parties' dollar selling and the U.S. unit's generally soft tone against regional currencies in intraday trading, they said.  

Government bond prices ended lower, in line with movement in the U.S. Treasury market since late Friday following stronger-than-expected U.S. retail sales data.  

Thai financial markets were closed Monday for a public holiday.  

The dollar ended at THB37.46, up from THB37.36 at the Asian close Friday, after moving in a range of THB37.36-THB37.46.  

"The dollar shot up on news that the central bank had entered the market. However, the verbal intervention couldn't spur a sharp rally as some offshore parties unloaded dollars in the afternoon," said a dealer at a local bank.  

Bank of Thailand Governor Pridiyathorn Devakula said Tuesday the baht was too strong and that the central bank had stepped in during the day to curb the currency's rise.  

"The baht is slightly too strong. We will ensure that it weakens slightly, but we will not oppose the baht's market trend," Pridiyathorn said.  

The governor said there were hefty equity-related inflows Friday, which were partially responsible for the baht's strength.  

Traders expect the dollar's immediate resistance at THB37.50 to cap the upside in the short term while support is pegged around THB37.35, where the central bank is expected to take action to limit the baht's rise.  

The baht has been outperforming regional currencies so far this year with a rise of about 11%. JPMorgan said in a report Monday, however, that although Bank of Thailand may intervene to limit the baht's gains, it is unlikely to try to reverse those gains because the strength of the baht helps weaken the passthrough to local inflation from higher global oil prices. [ 15-08-06 1045GMT ]  

The Thai government bond yields rose slightly, playing catch up with increases in U.S. Treasury yields late Friday and Monday on signs of strength in the U.S. economy, dealers said.  

However, strong demand in Tuesday's central bank bond auction helped take some of the yields off their early highs.  

Investors will be watching demand and yield levels in Wednesday's auction of 20-year bonds, as moderate local supply conditions will likely continue to mute the effects of recent increases in U.S. yields.  

Bank of Thailand sold at auction Tuesday THB10 billion worth of its 364-day bonds at an average 5.18887%, down from 5.20967% at last week's auction in line with secondary market bid levels.  

The average bid on the government bond due November 2009 rose two basis points to 5.316%, the July 2016 bid was up three basis points to 5.507% and the July 2026 bid added two basis points to end at 5.794%, according to the Web site of the Thai Bond Market Association.  

The most-active overnight interbank interest rate was expected to have remained in its recent range of 4.94%-4.95%.

title: Thai Baht Ends Up, Hits 6.5-Yr High; Short-End Bonds Up
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht extended its rally to end just off a six-and-a-half year high Friday as a torrent of offshore selling continued to weaken the dollar despite suspected intervention by the Bank of Thailand, traders said.  

Thai long-term government bonds were mostly unchanged, but prices of short-term treasury bills rose due to expectations that interest rates have peaked. The pressure from the short end caused prices of some medium-term bonds to rise as well.  

The dollar ended at THB37.36, down from THB37.46 at the Asian close Thursday.  

Offshore players continued to dump the dollar, which has been on a losing streak against regional currencies recently due to expectations that U.S. interest rates may have peaked.  

The dollar slid to THB37.28 in the afternoon, its lowest level since January 2000. It reached an intraday high of THB37.44 in the morning.  

But the U.S. unit staged a good recovery in late trade due to buying that was likely a combination of central bank action and players' adjustments to the dollar's rebound against key Asian currencies like the Japanese yen.  

Traders suspect Bank of Thailand once again bought dollars to help limit the baht's strength. Governor Pridiyathorn Devakula confirmed late Thursday that the central bank had been active in the market. Traders said the greenback could sink to THB37.15 in foreign markets over the long weekend with the local market closed Monday for a public holiday, unless the central bank continues to intervene.  

"If the central bank steps in during the holiday, support (for the dollar-baht exchange rate) would be around THB37.23-THB37.30," said a local trader. "If not, it could fall to THB37.15 by Tuesday morning."  

Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya attempted to assist the central bank with some mild verbal intervention Friday by saying the baht's strength during the past 2-3 days is likely a short term situation, and that the central bank has the means to temper the effects of volatile capital flows.  

"There is no unusual movement in the market. The central bank is also monitoring the market closely," Thanong told reporters. [ 11-08-06 1103GMT ]  

The Thai government bond yield curve steepened slightly due to demand for short-term paper on a market view that local interest rates have peaked, dealers said.  

Medium-term yields eased slightly under the pull of short-term yields, but except for the very shortest terms, declines were limited to one basis point.  

Further declines in short- and medium-term yields might follow if demand is as strong as expected at Tuesday's auction of THB10 billion worth of 364-day central bank bonds.  

The 364-day term was bid Friday at 5.19%, down from 5.20% Thursday, while the bid on 182-day paper eased to 4.98% from 4.99%.  

Earlier Friday, the Bank of Thailand sold THB6 billion worth of 28-day treasury bills at 4.78990%, down from an average of 4.84283% at Monday's auction. Another THB7 billion of 91-day t-bills was sold at an average 4.86644%, down from 4.90111%. But THB7 billion of 182-day t-bills was sold at an average 4.98429%, up marginally from 4.98053%.  

The average bid on the government bond due November 2009 fell one and 1/2 basis points to 5.298%, the July 2016 bid was almost flat at 5.474%, and the July 2026 bid was nearly unchanged at 5.771%, according to the Web site of the Thai Bond Market Association.  

The most-active overnight interbank interest rate was expected to have remained in its recent range of 4.94%-4.95%.

title: Thai baht at strongest since early 2000
text:
SINGAPORE, Aug 11 (Reuters) - The Thai baht rose to its highest level against the dollar since early 2000 on Friday and dealers said they were watching for central bank intervention to halt its rise.  

Dealers said general strength in Asian currencies, expectations of a faster appreciation in the Chinese yuan <CNY=CFXS> and flows into the local stock market all bolstered the baht.  

It went as high as 37.35 to the U.S. dollar <THB=>, its highest since February 2000, according to Reuters data.  

It is Asia's best performing currency this year with a gain of almost 10 percent.  

"The Thai baht is higher, partly because of the regional trend, partly because of the yuan," said a Bangkok trader.  

He said the market was wary of central bank intervention to cap the baht's gains but that there had been no sign of central bank activity in early trade.  

The Bank of Thailand said on Thursday it had intervened to slow the baht's rise against the dollar.  

Some analysts said that a comment by Governor Pridiyathorn Devakula that the baht was unlikely to return to levels of 38 to 39 per dollar suggested the central bank would tolerate currency strength to a certain degree.  

"The central bank is closely watching the market but it can't go against the trend," the trader said. "It just doesn't want to see volatile moves."

title: UPDATE 1-Thai  central bank intervenes  to slow baht rise
text:
(Adds quotes)  

BANGKOK, Aug 10 (Reuters) - The Bank of Thailand intervened to slow the baht's rise against the dollar on Thursday, but does not expect the Thai currency to return to levels of 38 to 39 per dollar, governor Pridiyathorn Devakula said.  

The central bank's action was intended mainly to smooth out baht volatility without trying to resist the broad market trend, he said.  

"We have entered the market today to try to ease its volatility. But at the same time, we need to look at the global picture," Pridiyathorn told reporters.  

Asked if the baht might soon return to the 38 per dollar level last seen on July 26 or the 39 to the dollar last hit on March 24, he said: "That is wishful thinking."  

The baht, the best performing Asian currency this year, rose about 0.49 percent in late trade to around 37.43 per dollar. It has strengthened about 9.85 percent this year.  

It's sustained strength since early this year did not seem to have hurt Thai exports which increased 17.1 percent during the first half of 2006 compared with the same period of 2005, Pridiyathorn said.

title: Thai Ctrl Bk Chief:US Deficits May Cause Rapid Cap Flows
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--A widening of U.S. deficits could spur a new round of rapid massive capital movements, but the Thai central bank said Wednesday that it is prepared for such an eventuality.  

Governor Pridiyathorn Devakula declined to say if the Bank of Thailand had in mind an intervention in the foreign exchange markets or something more than that. [ 09-08-06 0356GMT ]  

"We have our measures ready should there be any sudden drop in the value of the dollar," Pridiyathorn said.  

In the first four months of this year, funds flowed out of U.S. assets into other regions, including Asia, on concerns over a slowing U.S. economy. But soon after, substantial capital returned to the U.S. markets on investors' increased aversion to assets in emerging markets. This cycle has been repeated in the past few months, he said.  

On the baht, Pridiyathorn said that while the central bank intends to manage the currency to keep it at a level that would help exporters, it won't resist the baht's market trend.  

He also said that exporters should brace themselves for a firmer baht and shouldn't 'fancy' that the currency will ease to around THB40 against the dollar anytime soon.Around 0510 GMT, the dollar was at THB37.65, down slightly from THB37.70 in late trading Tuesday.  

Thailand's economic fundamentals remain strong, and private investment should resume oncea new government is in place, he said.  

He reiterated the central bank's forecast that the Thai economy will grow by 4.0%-5.0% this year and by 4.0%-5.25% next year.  

"Although the projected growth rates are not that high, they are considered satisfactory under the current situation," he said.  

But he allayed fears that the economy might face a new round of crisis, given the level of the country's foreign reserves - around $60 billion - and a strong growth in exports.  

Thailand faced a massive economic crisis in 1997, brought on by a depletion of the country's foreign reserves after a failed defense of its fixed exchange-rate mechanism.

title: Thai Baht Ends Higher On Broad Dlr Weakness; Bonds Up
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht ended higher Wednesday on dollar selling by offshore players amid broad weakness in the U.S. unit versus Asian currencies, but suspected intervention by the Bank of Thailand helped cap the baht's rise, traders said.  

Government bond prices closed slightly higher after an auction showed that demand remains firm relative to moderate supply.  

The dollar ended at THB37.82, down from THB38.23 at Tuesday's close.  

The U.S. unit hit its intraday high of THB38.02 in the morning, and was then dragged down by offshore selling.  

Traders said hedge funds squared long-dollar positions built up as the U.S. currency was rising over the past two days, prompting other players to join the selling.  

Weaker-than-expected U.S. housing data was a key reason for the reversal Wednesday of the dollar's rebound this week against major currencies.  

The greenback fell to an intraday low of THB37.73 in late trade.  

"But it rebounded just before the market close, possibly on buying by the Thai central bank," a trader at a local bank said.  

The dollar is expected to trade between THB37.70 and THB38.15 overnight. [ 17-05-06 1031GMT ]  

Most Thai government bond yields ended slightly lower as Wednesday's auction showed that domestic demand remains firm and the baht's rebound raised the prospect of foreign demand returning, dealers said.  

Buying by the central bank from primary dealers Tuesday also continued to support market sentiment.  

Bank of Thailand sold Wednesday THB3.4 billion of the government bond due May 2009 at an average 5.3539%, up from 5.3145% at last week's auction. The increase wasn't as much as feared however, and high bid coverage at 5.63 times confirmed that demand was very strong relative to supply.  

Another THB2.5 billion of the bond due March 2021 was sold at an average 5.8813%, down from 5.9135% at the previous offering of the issue on April 26.  

The average secondary market bid on the May 2009 issue was down two basis points at 5.330% and the July 2013 bid eased one basis point to 5.447%, while the July 2016 bid fell one basis point to 5.553% and the March 2021 bid dropped one and 1/2 basis points to end at 5.893%, according to the Web site of the Thai Bond Market Association.  

Dealers said yields could resume rising if the baht starts to weaken again or U.S. consumer price inflation data due later Wednesday indicates that U.S. and local interest rates will rise further than expected. But otherwise the mild downward correction of the increases seen earlier this week is likely to continue.  

The most-active overnight money market interest rate was expected to have remained at 4.65%.

title: Emerging Asia  FX -Month-long rally stalls
text:
SINGAPORE, May 4 (Reuters) - The Thai baht fell to a two-week low on Thursday while the Singapore dollar, South Korean won and Malaysian ringgit retreated from their highest levels in eight years as traders locked in profits from a one-month rally.  

The baht <THB=> and won <KRW=> both lost as much as three-quarters of a percent while the Singapore dollar <SGD=> and Philippine peso <PHP=> lost as much as half a percent.  

With Japan and China shut until the end of the week and financial markets in South Korea, Hong Kong and Thailand also closed on Friday, many traders decided to book profits from the Asian currency rally.  

Expectations of a faster appreciation in the Chinese yuan, fuelled by last week's surprise interest rate increase by China, had helped fuel the gains.  

But those expectations were doused by Chinese Vice Finance Minister Li Yong, who said in India on Thursday that China could not move too fast on the yuan.  

"China wants to tell everyone, 'don't get carried away by yuan talk'," said Jimmy Koh, currency strategist at United Overseas Bank in Singapore.  

"While everyone was expecting that China would do something with the yuan, China has not moved at all."  

The yuan has gained 1.2 percent since last July's revaluation, when China made the currency 2.1 percent stronger overnight and ended the currency's peg to the dollar.  

In contrast, the won and Thai baht have both surged more than 8 percent while the Singapore dollar and Malaysian ringgit have gained more than 4 percent over the same period. Koh said he expected trading in Asian currencies to be range-bound in coming weeks unless China moved decisively to let its currency appreciate at a faster pace.  

"Markets would want to see what China does after the holidays," he said.  

INTERVENTION WORRIES  

Traders refrained from bidding up Asian currencies after seeing widespread dollar buying by Asian central banks on Wednesday aimed at stifling sharp gains in their currencies.  

"Everybody's buying back dollars," said a Singapore currency dealer who said local banks, probably under orders from the central bank, had bid up the dollar in early morning trade.  

Asian finance ministers gathered in Hyderabad in India for an Asian Development Bank meeting sounded the alarm on the rapidly strengthening Asian currencies.  

South Korean Finance Minister Han Duck-soo said the won <KRW=> had overshot economic fundamentals and that the firmer currency and high oil prices were the main risks to the economy.  

Earlier, Japan's finance minister, Sadakazu Tanigaki, told reporters in Hyderabad that "currencies have been moving in a somewhat excessive manner".  

He said a statement issued by finance ministers of Group of Seven rich countries last month had been misunderstood by financial markets to mean the G7 favoured a dollar decline. He said any excessive currency movements were undesirable.  

In Thailand, data released on Thursday showed a $2.6 billion jump in foreign reserves between March 24 and April 28, confirming traders' talk that the Bank of Thailand (BOT) was intervening to stall the baht's gains.  

"We see the dollar/baht going slowly higher next week," said a dealer in Bangkok. "The BOT does not want a stronger baht."  

The baht weakened to a low of 37.89 per dollar. It has lost ground since hitting a six-year high of 37.40 per dollar on May 1 as soaring crude oil prices and political uncertainty finally took their toll.  

The baht climbed 3.6 percent in April and is up 8.9 percent so far this year, making it Asia's second-best performer.

title: Emerging Asia  FX - Intervention  as won, Sing dlr hit 8-year highs
text:
SINGAPORE, May 3 (Reuters) - The currencies of South Korea, Singapore and Malaysia hit their highest levels in more than eight years on Wednesday, prompting central bank intervention, as the U.S. dollar fell on speculation U.S. interest rates would stop rising soon.  

The won <KRW=> hit a high of 933.2 per dollar, its strongest level since October 1997.  

The Singapore dollar <SGD=> rose as high as 1.5730 per dollar, its highest since November 1997, while the Malaysian ringgit <MYR=> hit 3.6049 per dollar, a level last seen in April 1998.  

Traders said central banks across the region stepped in with dollar purchases to stifle further gains in their currencies. Some central banks intervened through state lenders.  

"The state-run banks have been buying dollars aggressively," said a Singapore currency dealer at a foreign bank.  

The dealer said investors held off from bidding the Singapore dollar higher after seeing the authorities intervene at 1.5730/35 levels. The currency could retreat to levels around 1.58 before traders pushed it higher again, dealers said.  

Similar intervention was noted in South Korea, Malaysia and Thailand.  

Asian authorities are worried that stronger currencies, could hurt Asian exports to the United States, Europe and Japan, particularly when China is keeping the yuan on a tight leash.  

Data on Wednesday indicated that the South Korean authorities had been intervening in the foreign exchange market since April. The country's foreign exchange reserves jumped $5.55 billion last month to $222.89 billion, the fourth largest in the world.  

"The authorities are afraid of the pace and further appreciation of the won. That's why they came into the market to support the dollar. But the intervention is a smoothing operation -- they want to moderate the pace and not stop the trend," said Roh Sang Chil, a currency trader at Kookmin Bank in Seoul.  

Swiss bank UBS said concerns about the record U.S. current account deficit, attempts by central banks to diversify their reserves away from the dollar and expectations that the Fed may end its rate-rise cycle after another increase this month were likely to dominate currency markets.  

It expects the yen <JPY=> to strengthen to 108 per dollar in three months from about 113.25 now. The euro <EUR=> could climb to $1.3 from about $1.26 over the same period, it said.  

TAIWAN INFLOWS  

The bearish dollar outlook and a surge in foreign investment in Taiwan's stock market helped push up the Taiwan dollar <TWD=TP> to a nine-month high of 31.59 per U.S. dollar.  

Foreign investors continued with their purchases of Taiwan stocks, picking up a net T$11.7 billion worth on Wednesday. They bought T$170 billion worth in April, the highest monthly total since December.  

The Philippine peso <PHP=> jumped more than half a percent to 51.32 per dollar, its strongest level in two weeks.  

The currency had tumbled to an eight-week low last week on concern about record high oil prices and the likely impact on the country's fiscal deficit but some analysts reasoned that strong remittances from overseas Filipino workers were likely to offset the outflow of dollars caused by soaring crude oil import costs. New York oil futures <CLc1> traded close to $75 per barrel, near last week's record high of $75.35.

title: Thai Baht Ends Flat,Off High On Oil Cos Buying;Bonds Flat
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht ended flat against the U.S. dollar in light trade Wednesday, with late buying mainly by oil companies wiping out early gains, dealers said.  

Thai government bond prices also ended flat in razor-thin trade as most investors were on the sidelines ahead of the long weekend. Thai markets will be closed Friday for a public holiday.  

The dollar ended at THB37.64, unchanged from Tuesday's close. The greenback opened softer at THB37.54 amid general dollar weakness against most regional currencies and gradually eased to an intraday low of THB37.49 in the afternoon.  

"However, dollar buying in late trade erased (the baht's) early gains after the dollar rebounded against other regional units. Besides, market participants are also cautious about possible intervention as the central bank seems to have stepped in several times to defend the THB37.50 level since last week," said a dealer at a local bank.  

Still, dealers said they don't detect any signs of possible intervention in recent sessions.  

Bank of Thailand's Governor Pridiyathorn Devakula said Wednesday the baht is starting to stabilize and that the bank did not intervene Tuesday to curb the currency's appreciation.  

The governor said capital continues to flow into the country in a "seeping" manner.  

The foreign exchange market didn't react much to the uncertainty in Thai politics Wednesday, as its movement was directed largely by that of regional units.  

The Thai Administrative Court said Wednesday it won't be able to rule on the validity of the April 2 elections until May 15. This will prolong the political uncertainty and delay the formation of new government.  

"Politics is largely discounted by the forex market. I think the market won't react until a concrete decision comes out," said another trader at a local bank.  

Traders expect the dollar to be held in a THB37.50-THB37.70 range Thursday. [ 03-05-06 1035GMT ]  

Thai government bond yields ended barely changed amid a holiday mood and lack of fresh factors, traders said.  

There was no bond auction Wednesday, and none will be held Thursday. The auction will resume next week.  

The average bid on the government bond due December 2008 was flat at 5.310%, while the July 2013 bid rose one basis point to 5.46%. The July 2016 bid and the March 2021 were both flat at 5.55% and 5.87% respectively, according to the Thai Bond Market Association's Web site.  

The overnight money market interest rate remained high as local banks kept high money reserves ahead of an upcoming long weekend.

title: Thai baht retreats as poll verdict, oil weigh
text:
SINGAPORE, May 2 (Reuters) - The Thai baht retreated on Tuesday from a six-year high hit the previous day as some traders expected the country's Constitutional court to scrap April's inconclusive general election, prolonging the political crisis.  

The currency was also weighed down by concerns about the impact of soaring oil prices on domestic consumption and inflation. The government said on Monday annual consumer price inflation accelerated unexpectedly in April from March, putting further pressure on the central bank to raise rates.  

The baht <THB=> weakened to the day's low of 37.69 per dollar, down half a percent from Friday.  

Financial markets were closed on Monday when the Constitutional Court agreed to hear a petition by law lecturers and a civic group to annul the April 2 general election.  

Traders said the political uncertainty, near-record high oil prices, rising inflation and a slowing economy all combined to encourage traders to bid for dollars. The dollar's rebound against the yen also helped push up the U.S. currency against the baht, they said.  

"The economy is now calming down because inflation is higher due to oil prices. People are not willing to invest much," said a Bangkok-based currency dealer.  

Meanwhile, Bank of Thailand was seen buying dollars last week to stifle the baht's gains despite the worsening outlook for the economy.  

The baht has climbed 9 percent this year, making it the second best performing currency in Asia after the Indonesian rupiah <IDR=>.  

IDEAGlobal said in a report it expected Bank of Thailand to step up its intervention against the baht's gains, given the currency's strong performance this year. It pointed to the latest reserves data, which it said indicated central bank interventions.  

Thailand's foreign reserves rose by $2 billion to $56.6 billion between March 24 and April 21, according to the latest data disclosed by the central bank. ((Editing by Alex Richardson; rajat.bhattacharya@reuters.com; Reuters Messaging: rajat.bhattacharya.reuters.com@reuters.net; +65 6870 3841))

title: Thai Baht Ends Up On Broad Dollar Weakness; Bonds Jump
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht ended higher against the dollar Friday in line with broad weakness in the U.S. unit but suspected intervention by the Bank of Thailand helped limit the dollar losses, traders said.  

Traders said the latest political developments and economic data from the central bank had little impact on the baht amid thin trade ahead of a long weekend.  

Government bond prices finished sharply higher on hefty buying interest spurred by the view that the domestic interest rate tightening cycle may soon end.  

The dollar ended at THB37.50, down from THB37.59 at Thursday's close after it slid to a fresh six-year low of THB37.46 in the morning.  

Traders said the dollar was tracking its decline against other regional currencies in the morning.  

"However, the greenback rebounded later on suspected buying by the central bank when it dipped to THB37.46," a local trader said.  

"The market is rather quiet in a holiday mood despite the development on political fronts," he said.  

Thai markets will be closed Monday for the Labor Day holiday.  

The Administrative Court canceled a Saturday by-election to be held in 14 constituencies that remained undecided after inconclusive snap polls April 2.  

The ruling came hours after the country's top judges said they couldn't immediately rule on the validity of April 2 general elections, but vowed that a verdict would be delivered soon to steer the country out of a deepening political crisis.  

Meanwhile, the central bank said in the afternoon that Thailand swung to a trade surplus of $187 million in March due to strong export growth. The trade surplus, though lower than economists' expectations, had been expected.  

Traders said the dollar will move within a THB37.40-THB37.70 range in trading Tuesday. [ 28-04-06 1149GMT ]  

Government yields dropped significantly on active buying by both offshore parties and local funds, with the central bank also believed to have bought short-term bonds, traders said.  

Buying sprees were inspired by Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya's comment Thursday that current interest rate levels appeared to be sufficient to control inflation, they said.  

Traders said part of the capital inflows, which caused the recent baht rally, have been parked in bonds, driving bond demand further.  

"It's a herd behavior. It seems like the whole market is now on the buy side....I've also seen lots of buying orders from local units of foreign banks today," a local financial institution dealer said.  

Yields were also weighed by suspected buying by the central bank in short-term bonds, specifically in one- to three-year issues, during the morning session, traders said.  

The Bank of Thailand sold THB17 billion worth of treasury bills Friday at average yields which were slightly lower than those of its previous auction, due to a belief that the rising trend in interest rates is over or will soon end.  

The central bank sold THB6 billion of 28-day t-bills at an average accepted yield of 4.50667%, THB6 billion of 91-day t-bills at an average 4.67583%, and THB5 billion of 182-day t-bills at an average 4.86900%.  

The average bid on the government bond due August 2008 was down nine basis points at 5.242%, while the July 2013 bid plunged almost 10 basis points to 5.410%. The July 2016 bid tumbled 10 basis points to 5.506%, and the bid on the March 2021 issue dropped nine basis points to 5.824%, according to the Thai Bond Market Association's Web site.  

The overnight money market interest rate was up slightly at 4.67% due to month-end demand and preparation for Monday's holiday.

title: Thai Baht Ends Down;Oil Cos,Importers Buy Dlrs; Bonds Up
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht ended slightly lower against the U.S. dollar Friday on dollar buying by oil companies and local importers, traders said.  

The baht also eased on concerns over possible intervention by the Bank of Thailand to curb the currency's rise, they said.  

Government bonds ended higher, continuing their rebound after recent losses.  

The dollar ended at THB37.81, up from THB37.75 at Thursday's close. The U.S. unit traded between THB37.77 and THB37.89 Friday.  

Traders said the dollar rose to its intraday high in the morning, tracking a broad dollar rebound before selling by exporters trimmed gains.  

Although BOT intervention concerns are likely to continue supporting the dollar, exporters are ready to sell on any gains as most are not expecting a strong dollar recovery in the near term, dealers said.  

"The dollar was supported by demand from oil companies and importers. Trading volume was thin as many players stayed on the sidelines amid worries about possible central bank intervention," said a trader at a local bank.  

BOT Deputy Governor Bandid Nijathaworn said Thursday that the central bank is closely monitoring foreign exchange markets to ensure that the baht doesn't move excessively.  

Traders said they suspected that agents of the central bank have intervened in favor of the U.S. dollar on several occasions recently, but the BOT doesn't comment directly on current market operations.  

The dollar hit a six-year low at THB37.66 in offshore trade during a local holiday Wednesday.  

Traders expect the dollar to remain in a range of THB37.70-THB37.90 over the weekend. [ 21-04-06 1108GMT ]  

Government bond yields ended lower in a further downward correction following central bank intervention Thursday, dealers said.  

Demand in the long end of the curve outstrips moderate supply, and many investors think there may be only one more 25-basis point hike in the central bank's 14-day repurchase market target rate during the current tightening cycle.  

However, as the 14-day rate is now 4.75%, the downside for short and medium yields is likely to be limited.  

The average bid for the government bond due August 2008 eased four basis points to 5.410%, the December 2014 bid dropped five basis points to 5.662%, the July 2016 bid was down six basis points at 5.707% and the bid on the March 2021 issue fell six basis points to 6.061%, according to the Thai Bond Market Association's Web site.  

The overnight money market interest rate is expected to have remained around 4.63%.

title: Thai Baht Ends Up, Off Wednesday's 6-Yr High; Bonds Up
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht ended firmer against the U.S. dollar Thursday compared with the previous Bangkok close, but it was off the fresh six-year high set in offshore trade during the closure of local markets Wednesday, dealers said.  

Robust March trade data issued Thursday supported baht sentiment, but the effect was limited because the figures were in line with expectations and players were worried about possible central bank intervention in support of the dollar, they said.  

Government bond prices ended higher due to central bank buying. The intervention helped extend Tuesday's mild upward correction of sharp recent losses, which had been caused by rising interest rates.  

The dollar ended at THB37.75, down from THB37.98 at Tuesday's close in Asia but up from a fresh six-year low of THB37.66 reached Wednesday, when Thai financial markets were closed for a public holiday.  

The U.S. unit opened Thursday at THB37.78 and stayed in a tight range of THB37.71 to THB37.82.  

"The baht has rallied a long way now and many people are seeing only limited upside. Meanwhile, concerns that the central bank could step in anytime if the baht should rise further discouraged any attempt to drive the baht up significantly," said a dealer at a local bank.  

Bank Of Thailand Deputy Governor Bandid Nijathaworn said Thursday that the central bank is closely monitoring foreign exchange markets to ensure that the baht doesn't move excessively.  

"The point is that we don't want the baht to be too volatile," he told reporters.  

Foreign exchange traders said they suspected that agents of the central bank have intervened in favor of the U.S. dollar on several occasions recently, but the central bank doesn't comment directly on current market operations.  

Bandid said the baht's recent strength was in line with that of other Asian currencies, resulting from broad dollar weakness and capital inflows into the region.  

Thailand posted a customs-basis trade surplus of $324.5 million in March, ending a string of deficits since December, due mainly to strong growth in exports of agricultural and automotive products, the Ministry of Commerce said Thursday.  

Exports in March grew 15.9% on year to $11.10 billion, while imports rose 1.3% to $10.78 billion. The preliminary figures are based on data from the customs department. Official data is due April 28 from the central bank, excluding goods in transit and including some goods which don't pass through customs.  

Dealers expected the dollar to trade in a range of THB37.70-THB37.85 overnight. [ 20-04-06 1114GMT ]  

Government bond yields ended lower after central bank buying extended a downward correction that began Tuesday, when a weekly auction showed that demand continued to outstrip moderate supply, dealers said.  

Bank of Thailand intervened to buy bonds maturing in 10-15 years, and the effect was exaggerated in light trading volume, they said.  

The downside for yields is likely to be limited, however, as many investors still expect one more 25-basis point increase in the current tightening cycle in the central bank's 14-day repurchase market target rate, which is currently 4.75%.  

The average bid for the government bond due August 2008 fell five basis points to 5.447%, while the December 2014 bid plunged 11 basis points to 5.711%, the July 2016 bid skidded 11 basis points to 5.763% and the bid on the March 2021 issue dropped seven basis points to end at 6.123%, according to the Thai Bond Market Association's Web site.  

The overnight money market interest rate was expected to have remained around 4.63%.

title: Emerging Asia  FX -Central banks act to limit gains
text:
SINGAPORE, April 18 (Reuters) - Several Asian central banks were suspected of intervening on Tuesday to hold down their currencies, which had risen initially because of a growing view that U.S. interest rate increases could be near an end.  

The South Korean won <KRW=> rose as high as 951.8 per dollar and then retreated on worries about possible central bank intervention. Data on Tuesday showing currency reserves had increased in the first half of April underpinned those concerns.  

The Thai baht <THB=> was quoted briefly at a six-year high of 37.85 per dollar but its gains were pared after some dealers spoke of possible dollar buying by the Bank of Thailand on Monday and Tuesday. Verbal intervention by central bank authorities last week also made traders wary.  

The Singapore dollar extended recent gains to 1.5999 per U.S. dollar <SGD=>, its strongest level in nearly eight years, before pulling back after dollar purchases by local banks, which dealers suspected were on behalf of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).  

"To a degree the price move reflects broader dollar trends, but market participants also appear to be testing out how low they can take U.S. dollar/Sing dollar before the MAS reacts aggressively intervention-wise," Lim Su Sian, an economist at the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, said in a note.  

However, Lim said the MAS seemed to be merely providing some defence for the U.S. dollar at the 1.6000 level rather than aggressively attempting to reverse the market's direction.  

Last Tuesday, the MAS stuck to a policy of gradual currency appreciation, surprising markets who were looking for it to allow a bigger rise in the trade-weighted Singapore dollar. The MAS conducts monetary policy by steering the local currency within an undisclosed band based on a trade-weighted basket of currencies.  

Some analysts said the Sing dollar's rise since the decision suggested the current policy permitted it to have a wider band and a steeper appreciation than most believed.  

DOLLAR TREND  

Apart from the won, which retained some of its gains, most of the Asian currencies were either down or barely changed on the day, even though the U.S. dollar stayed soft against the yen <JPY=> and euro <EUR=>.  

Some of the early gains had come from expectations of an end to U.S. rate rises. Analysts said minutes from the Fed's March meeting and U.S. March housing data due later on Tuesday would be watched for further clues on rates.  

Traders said there was still some interest in buying the Asian currencies ahead of Chinese President Hu Jintao's visit to Washington this week, when he will come under pressure to allow the yuan to appreciate more rapidly.  

"It keeps bubbling in the background and is acting as a cap on dollar/Asia, but expectations are relatively low that there will be a huge announcement from Hu," said Westpac senior currency strategist Sean Callow.  

But Hu was unlikely to say anything that would dash all expectations of yuan appreciation, particularly while in the United States, where he would be facing heavy pressure to do something to tackle global trade imbalances, Callow said.

Government bond prices closed higher, recovering some recent losses after an auction showed that demand for long-term issues remains strong amid moderate supply.  

The dollar ended at THB37.98, up from THB37.93 at Monday's close in Asia.  

The U.S. unit eased to THB37.89 in the morning, in line with its regional trend, after rising against the trend overnight to a high of THB38.09.  

Some traders suspected that the Bank of Thailand was behind the dollar's gains overnight, ahead of a meeting Tuesday with caretaker Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya, who had expressed concern about the possible effect of the baht's gains on exports.  

However, Thanong said after meeting central bank officials Tuesday that he wasn't worried about the baht's strength, as the local unit has been supported by capital inflows into Thai assets.  

Caretaker Commerce Minister Somkid Jatusripitak said late Monday that March exports likely exceeded $10 billion, after rising 23.3% on year to $9.43 billion in February.  

Traders said a mild recovery by the dollar against other Asian currencies Tuesday afternoon prompted buying on weakness against the baht by foreign players, but the dollar's rise was capped at an intraday high of THB37.99 due to selling by local exporters.  

Traders expect the dollar to hover in the THB37.90-THB38.00 range overnight and in offshore trade Wednesday. Thai financial markets will be closed Wednesday for a public holiday. [ 18-04-06 1120GMT ]

The bias for yields remains upward, in line with the trend in interest rates, but dealers generally agreed with Thanong, who said Tuesday that the central bank's 14-day repurchase market target rate is likely near its peak after last week's 25-basis point hike to 4.75%.

BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht ended slightly lower against the U.S. dollar Tuesday on offshore dollar buying in late trade after suspected intervention by the Bank of Thailand overnight, traders said.  

Government bond prices closed higher, recovering some recent losses after an auction showed that demand for long-term issues remains strong amid moderate supply.  

The dollar ended at THB37.98, up from THB37.93 at Monday's close in Asia.  

The U.S. unit eased to THB37.89 in the morning, in line with its regional trend, after rising against the trend overnight to a high of THB38.09.  

Some traders suspected that the Bank of Thailand was behind the dollar's gains overnight, ahead of a meeting Tuesday with caretaker Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya, who had expressed concern about the possible effect of the baht's gains on exports.  

However, Thanong said after meeting central bank officials Tuesday that he wasn't worried about the baht's strength, as the local unit has been supported by capital inflows into Thai assets.  

Caretaker Commerce Minister Somkid Jatusripitak said late Monday that March exports likely exceeded $10 billion, after rising 23.3% on year to $9.43 billion in February.  

Traders said a mild recovery by the dollar against other Asian currencies Tuesday afternoon prompted buying on weakness against the baht by foreign players, but the dollar's rise was capped at an intraday high of THB37.99 due to selling by local exporters.  

Traders expect the dollar to hover in the THB37.90-THB38.00 range overnight and in offshore trade Wednesday. Thai financial markets will be closed Wednesday for a public holiday.

title: Thai Baht Ends Down On Dollar Short Covering; Bonds Flat
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht ended softer against the U.S. dollar Wednesday on suspected intervention, hefty dollar buying by oil companies and dollar short covering by interbank players in a bid to limit exposures ahead of a long holiday weekend in Thailand, dealers said.  

Government bonds ended virtually flat in thin trade amid the holiday lull, as the country's financial markets will be closed Thursday and Friday for the traditional New Year's break.  

The dollar ended at THB38.13, up from THB38.03 at Tuesday's close in Asia. The U.S. unit opened lower at THB37.96, following its losses earlier against the Singapore dollar.  

It fell to an intraday low of THB37.95, where the central bank is suspected to have stepped in to curb the baht's strength. The dollar shot to an intraday high of THB38.18 before selling by exporters capped gains.  

"Oil companies actively sought dollars to settle their business obligations. As the dollar rebounded, many interbank players also bought dollars to cover short in order to square out or trim their positions ahead of the upcoming long holidays," said a dealer at a local bank.  

Despite suspected intervention, Bank of Thailand Assistant Governor Atchana Waiquamdee said Wednesday the central bank couldn't intervene much in the market to help stop the baht strengthening.  

"We can't set the market. We have to let the baht move in line with the market mechanism," Atchana said.  

She said the baht's strength was due to continued capital inflows and improved sentiment resulting from easing political concerns.  

"Don't look at baht strength as a key negative factor for exports. The main issue for exporters is their productivity. Actually, a strong baht helps the country a lot in terms of a lower value for oil imports," she said.  

Bank of Thailand Governor Pridiyathorn Devakula said Wednesday that recent capital inflows, the key driver of strength in the Thai baht, were to buy stocks rather than for speculation.  

"The current baht level is slightly stronger than other (regional) currencies thanks to huge capital inflows earlier in the year. But we think it will stabilize after this," Pridiyathorn said.  

Pridiyathorn said the current baht level is still competitive for exports, considering the recent strong export figures.  

The central bank was suspected of intervening repeatedly in the market since last Friday.  

Traders expect the dollar to find support at THB37.90, where the central bank is believed to take action, while firm resistance is pegged at THB38.30. [ 12-04-06 1020GMT ]  

Government bond yields ended almost flat, as many players were away ahead of the holiday.  

Traders said the Bank of Thailand tapped into the sleepy market, buying some long-term bonds with 10-year to 17-year maturities. Though the move helped limit rises in yields, it hardly stirred follow-through buying.  

The average bid for government bonds due December 2014 was up one basis point at 5.779%, while bids on the March 2012 issue rose one basis point to 5.656%, and bids on the March 2021 issue were flat at 6.136%, according to Thai Bond Market Association's Web site.  

The money market was also rather quiet ahead of the holiday, with interest rates mostly flat.

title: Thai Baht Ends Off High On Possible  Intervention ;Bonds Dn
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht was higher against the dollar late Tuesday on gains in some regional currencies and equity-related inflows, traders said.  

However, the baht's rise was apparently capped by continued dollar buying by the Bank of Thailand, traders suspected.  

Government bond prices were quoted lower in line with the rising interest rate trend, but trading was razor-thin as most players were on the sidelines ahead of a long holiday for Thailand's traditional new year.  

The dollar ended at THB38.03, down from THB38.14 at Monday's close in Asia. The U.S. unit spiraled down to a fresh six-year low of THB37.92 before noon. The intraday low was the lowest since April 2000, beating Monday's record of THB37.98.  

The U.S. unit clung around its intraday high of THB38.05 in the morning, then continued its retreat.  

"The dollar's slide was more in line with its losses against the yuan and the Singapore dollar than the dollar-yen, while the (equity) inflows remained supportive to the baht," said a local trader.  

Soon after it dived to the intraday low, the dollar bounced back.  

Traders said the central bank may have stepped in around THB37.95, although its authorities avoided mentioning any intervention when asked by reporters.  

Bank of Thailand Deputy Governor Bandid Nijathaworn said that the Thai baht's current strength was mainly due to steady capital inflows.  

However, the central bank hasn't determined whether those inflows are for investment or for speculation, Bandid told reporters.  

"We will monitor the market closely to make sure that the baht is not too strong," he said, but added that his remarks weren't meant to suggest the central bank is directly intervening in the market at the moment.  

Bandid's remark followed comments by Bank of Thailand Governor Pridayathorn Devakula, who said earlier Tuesday that the baht exchange rate moved in line with regional currencies.  

Traders expect that the dollar's support at THB37.95 should hold Wednesday morning, with resistance at THB38.10. [ 11-04-06 1022GMT ]  

Government bond yields ended higher in a wide bid-offer range amid very thin trade due to upcoming long holidays and a large number of auctions in the primary market, traders said.  

Thai financial markets will be closed on Thursday and Friday for public holidays.  

"There were few deals done as most investors paid attention to the primary market rather than the secondary market," said a local bank trader.  

There were three auctions on Tuesday - state enterprise bonds, central bank bonds and government bonds - with a combined value of around THB16 billion.  

Thailand's Ministry of Finance sold THB500 million of eight-year Expressway & Rapid Transit Authority, or ETA, bonds at auction Tuesday with an accepted yield of 5.83%, as well as THB1 billion of nine-year ETA bonds at 5.89%.  

The accepted yields represented premiums of around 14-17 basis points over the government bond yield curve. Despite the government guarantee, the premiums were wider than normal, which is around 10-12 basis points, due to the long maturity.  

The Bank of Thailand sold THB12 billion worth of its 363-day central bank bonds in an auction at 5.29190%, up from 5.19392% at last week's auction.  

The central bank also sold THB2.5 billion of government bonds due March 2021 at 6.0907%, with a bid coverage ratio of 2.58 times.  

The average bid for government bonds due August 2008 was up four basis points at 5.436%, while the bid on the July 2013 issue rose five basis points to 5.695%. The July 2016 bid was up six basis points to 5.808%, and the bid on the March 2021 issue was up seven basis points to end at 6.130%, according to Thai Bond Market Association's Web site.  

The most active overnight interbank rate rose slightly due to tight liquidity ahead of the long holidays.

title: Thai Baht Ends Up On Inflows But Off 6-Yr High; Bonds Dn
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht rallied further Friday on continued portfolio inflows amid easing political tension following Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra's decision to step down, dealers said.  

They said they suspected that central bank intervention brought the baht off a fresh six-year high but Bank of Thailand Governor Pridiyathorn Devakula denied the authority had intervened.  

Government bond prices edged lower in cautious trade ahead of Monday's monetary policy committee meeting, when the central bank's 14-day repurchase market target rate is widely expected to rise 25 basis points to 4.75%.  

The dollar ended at THB38.19, down from THB38.39 at Wednesday's close in Asia. Thai financial markets were closed Thursday for a public holiday. The U.S. unit plunged mid-afternoon to a fresh six-year low of THB38.06, the lowest level since May 2000.  

Thaksin said Tuesday that he wouldn't take the prime minister's post in the next government, likely to be formed around the end of the month following snap elections on April 2.  

"The baht was boosted by portfolio inflows. Easing worries on the political front are making foreign investors return to Thailand, at least for the time being," said a dealer at a local bank.  

The Stock Exchange of Thailand index ended up 3.1% Wednesday, with foreign investors buying a net THB15 billion.  

The dollar was also weighed down by exporter sales amid fears that the U.S. unit could fall further, dealers said.  

The baht's rise was also supported by Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya's comment Friday that a dollar rate of around THB38.00 is in line with regional units and not considered too strong. However, Thanong said any further slump in the dollar could pose a serious concern, citing an analyst's forecast suggesting the dollar may fall by another 30% against major currencies given the fundamentals of the U.S. economy.  

Dealers said the dollar's fall was limited by suspected intervention by the Bank of Thailand.  

"It seems very clear that the authority has stepped in. Without such a move, the dollar would have dropped more," said another dealer.  

However, the Bank of Thailand's Governor Pridiyathorn Devakula said late Friday the central bank hadn't intervened to curb the recent strength of the baht.  

"The baht strength is due to investor confidence (in the Thai economy)," he told reporters.  

Traders expect the dollar to test firm psychological support at THB38.00 next week, while initial resistance is pegged at THB38.30. [ 07-04-06 1113GMT ]  

Government bond yields ended higher in very thin trade ahead of the interest rate increase expected next week, but only slightly higher as the likely rise of 25 basis points was largely factored into the market, dealers said.  

The Thai Bond Market Association said the average bid yield on the government bond due August 2008 was almost unchanged at 5.386%, while the bid on the July 2013 issue edged up one basis point to 5.627%. The July 2016 bid added one basis point to 5.719%, and the bid on the new March 2021 issue was up one basis point to end at 6.024%.  

The most-active overnight interbank rate was expected to have remained around 4.37%. Dealers said the most-active level has declined this week from levels around 4.40% because banks are keeping extra cash in the overnight term to keep it available for investment in the higher 14-day rate expected Monday afternoon.

title: Thai Baht Ends Up As PM Decides To Step Down; Bonds Mixed
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht finished higher against the U.S. dollar Wednesday, as Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra's decision to step down appeared to break the political impasse that has haunted the local currency for months, traders said.  

However, the baht ended off a one-year high on suspected intervention by the Bank of Thailand and the dollar's intraday rebound against other regional currencies, they said.  

Government bond prices ended mixed as the yield curve continued to flatten under pressure from expectations the Bank of Thailand will on Monday raise its 14-day repurchase market target rate by 25 basis points to 4.75%.  

The dollar ended at THB38.39, down from THB38.64 at Tuesday's close in Asia.  

The U.S. unit plunged to a one-year low of THB38.25 in the morning after Thaksin said Tuesday night he wouldn't take the prime minister's post in the next government, likely to be formed around the end of the month following snap elections on April 2.  

Organizers of anti-Thaksin protests and key opposition parties said they generally accepted Thaksin's decision.  

"Thaksin's move lifted huge pressure on the baht and triggered heavy baht-buying by local and foreign players," said a local trader.  

Strong foreign buying in Thai shares also hammered the dollar, traders said.  

The Stock Exchange of Thailand index ended up 3.1% Wednesday on a huge trading value of THB51.07 billion.  

But the U.S. unit proved resilient. It bounced back against regional units, pulling the dollar-baht off lows.  

"There was dollar short-covering in the afternoon in line with the its movement against some Asian units," said another trader.  

Traders also said the Bank of Thailand might have stepped in to stem the baht's surge in the afternoon, fueling the dollar's rebound.  

The central bank seemed to have come in at THB38.30, they said.  

Aside from concern about the central bank, investors may have also begun to consider the various unknowns in Thaksin's plan. By-elections for seats left unfilled in Sunday's elections could delay the opening of the legislature, and if Thaksin tries to assume an active role in the next government outside of the premiership, mass protests against him may continue.  

Traders expected the dollar to swing in the THB38.25-THB38.48 range overnight, subject to a rate decision overnight by the European Central Bank and its impact on Asian currencies.  

Thai markets are closed Thursday for a public holiday. [ 05-04-06 1043GMT ]  

Government bond yields ended mixed, as the long end of the curve has apparently priced in the expected interest rate increase, while medium-term yields continued to edge higher, dealers said.  

The Thai Bond Market Association said the average bid yield on the government bond due November 2009 was up two basis points to 5.463%, and the bid on the March 2012 bond added one basis point to 5.543%. But the July 2013 bid eased one basis point to 5.613%, the July 2016 bid dropped one basis point to 5.717%, and the bid on the new March 2021 issue slipped two basis points to end at 6.012%.  

Political uncertainty had a very limited effect on the market, as movement has been dominated by interest rate expectations, dealers said.  

The most-active overnight interbank rate was expected to have remained around 4.39%-4.40%, with a downward bias after slipping to 4.39% Tuesday. Banks have been preparing cash for extra demand over several holidays this month and for investment Monday at the higher rate expected in the 14-day repurchase market term.

title: Thai Ctrl Bk Chief:  Intervened  To Cap Baht Rise Monday
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--Thailand's central bank intervened in the foreign exchange market Monday to limit the strength of the baht, Bank of Thailand Governor Pridiyathorn Devakula said late Tuesday.  

"We stepped in to manage (the baht) slightly Monday, but we didn't do anything today, just let it moves in line with the market," Pridiyathorn told reporters. [ 21-03-06 1107GMT ]  

The dollar weakened sharply Monday to end at THB38.625, down from THB39.02 at Friday's close in Asia and THB38.84 early Monday, catching up with last week's fall in the dollar-yen pair. Pridiyathorn didn't elaborate on the extent of Monday's intervention, which would have curbed the losses in the dollar.  

The U.S. currency ended higher Tuesday, reaching THB38.83 at the Asian close, boosted by importers' demand for the U.S. unit and tracking the dollar's rebound against regional currencies.  

The central bank's assistant governor, Atchana Waiquamdee, told reporters Tuesday that the dollar weakened Monday due to recent poor U.S. economic data, which has sparked concerns that the Federal Reserve will soon end its tightening cycle.  

"But the dollar recovered today, making the baht weaker, after Bernanke's comment this morning," Atchana said.  

U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke said the current flatness of the U.S. Treasury yield curve doesn't signal an impending slowdown in the U.S. economy.  

Market players viewed Bernanke's speech as slightly hawkish despite the absence of an outlook for monetary policy, traders said.  

Bernanke's speech "was noncommittal, which meant overall he made the case for the market to stay where it is," said Claudio Piron, currency strategist at JPMorgan.

title: Thai Baht Ends Dn On Political Worries; Bonds Higher
text:
BANGKOK (Dow Jones)--The Thai baht ended lower against the U.S. dollar in thin Asian spot trade Monday due to offshore dollar buying prompted by concerns over the stability of the Thai government, traders said.  

Long-term government bond prices rose following developments which took place Friday, including a rise in U.S.Treasurys and central bank buying in the Thai market.  

The dollar ended at THB39.36, up from THB39.29 at Friday's Asian close.  

The U.S. unit traded early Monday around the intraday low of THB39.18, tracking its weakness against other regional currencies. Foreigners began to pick up the dollar, however, after they were spooked by escalating political concerns.  

Efforts to oust Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra gained momentum after his influential political mentor, Chamlong Srimuang, called for him to quit and announced he would join a mass anti-Thaksin protest Sunday.  

Thaksin called an emergency Cabinet meeting Sunday night after Chamlong's announcement and told his ministers "he will not resign, but if the situation deteriorates, he will dissolve the parliament," said government spokesman Suraphong Suebwonglee.  

For the time being, the threat to dissolve the parliament appears to be a last resort, and a reminder to those opposed to Thaksin that his Thai Rak Thai Party would likely return to power with strong rural support. A move to dissolve the house would lead to new elections.  

The jitters were expected to continue weighing on the market while investors wait and see the strength and strategies of anti-Thaksin protesters at Sunday's rally.  

The dollar climbed to an intraday high of THB39.37 in the afternoon and remained near that level for the remainder of the Asian day.

The Ministry of Commerce said Monday that based on raw customs department data, the deficit in the country's balance of trade rose to $442 million in January from $142.1 million in December.  

But January import growth was at its lowest level in 43 months - at 2% on year - due mostly to lower oil imports after the elimination of a subsidy on retail prices in July of last year, and government pressure on the private sector to limit imports of oil, gold and steel.  

The U.S. unit is expected to trade overnight in a range of THB39.20-THB39.50, traders said. [ 20-02-06 1120GMT ]

The Thai Bond Market Association said the average bid yield on the government bond due August 2008 was nearly unchanged at 4.990%.
